SYSTEM NOTE · 01

ADAPTIVE TUTOR · AGES 2–3

A voice tutor that meets a child where they are.

The system does more than answer. It estimates what the child can do, selects one small learning step, watches the response, and adapts the next turn.

THE IMPORTANT LOOP

observe→estimate→teach→check→adapt

Hearing and speaking are the interface. The learner model and teaching policy make it a tutor.

01 / BASE ARCHITECTURE

Three inputs. Three decision systems. One short activity.

Keep the teaching logic separate from the voice model. A model can speak naturally. Your application must control what is taught, how difficulty changes, and what data is retained.

CHILD SIGNALS

What happened now

  • Spoken answer
  • Silence or interruption
  • Choice or tap
  • Time and retries
PARENT SETTINGS

What the adult controls

  • Language and interests
  • Approved learning goals
  • Session length
  • Data and privacy choices
→
01

GUARDIAN LAYER

Can this interaction happen?

Applies parent settings, content rules, session limits, and action permissions.

Tracks skill evidence, confidence, interests, and the current session state.

Selects the objective, prompt, scaffold, feedback, and difficulty adjustment.

OBSERVED EVIDENCE RETURNS TO THE LEARNER MODEL↩

02 / ADAPTIVE LOOP

The next turn depends on the last one.

Select a stage to see what the system decides. Each stage produces a small, testable output.

01 · OBSERVE

Collect evidence without judging too quickly.

Record the answer, response type, delay, retry count, and current activity. One response is evidence. It is not a permanent label.

INPUT
Child response + activity context
OUTPUT
Structured observation event
RULE
Keep raw evidence separate from skill estimates

03 / LEARNER MODEL

Track capabilities as evidence, not labels.

The learner model is a small data structure. It stores a skill estimate and confidence for each domain. It does not diagnose development.

DOMAINWHAT YOU OBSERVESTATE
Receptive language

Follows one-step prompts. Identifies familiar objects.

skill + confidence
Expressive language

Uses sounds, words, short phrases, or another response mode.

skill + confidence
Early concepts

Matches colors, shapes, quantities, animals, or familiar actions.

skill + confidence
Interaction pattern

Response mode, useful wait time, repetition needs, and interests.

session context

UPDATE RULE

prior state+new evidence→small update

Never make a large capability change from one answer. Use repeated, varied evidence across sessions.

04 / TEACHING POLICY

One observation can create different next turns.

TUTOR PROMPT

“Which one is the cat?”

OBSERVE

Child selects the cat.

→
ESTIMATE

Positive evidence for animal matching.

→
NEXT TURN

Confirm, then vary the example.

“Yes, that is the cat. Can you find another cat?”

05 / CHILD SAFETY

The guardian layer is part of the architecture.

This product is for very young children. Safety, parent control, and minimal data collection are system requirements, not later additions.

01

Adult remains in control

Parent setup, visible session state, stop control, and simple progress summaries.

02

Bounded content

Use reviewed activity templates. Limit open-ended generation and external tools.

03

No diagnosis

Describe observed learning evidence. Do not make medical or developmental conclusions.

04

Minimum necessary data

Prefer structured events over stored recordings. Give parents retention controls.

06 / FIRST BUILD

Prove the adaptive loop before building a curriculum.

Start with one learning domain, three activities, and three difficulty levels. Make the decision path visible in logs.

  1. 01

    Pick one skill

    Example: match red, blue, and yellow.

  2. 02

    Create reviewed templates

    Use fixed prompts, choices, hints, and feedback.

  3. 03

    Store evidence events

    Answer, delay, retries, scaffold used, and outcome.

  4. 04

    Implement three adaptations

    Easier, same level with variation, or one step harder.
